You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE players (
    player_id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name TEXT,
    last_name TEXT,
    hand TEXT,
    birth_date DATE,
    country_code TEXT,
    UNIQUE (player_id)
);

CREATE TABLE matches (
    best_of INT,
    draw_size INT,
    loser_age FLOAT,
    loser_entry TEXT,
    loser_hand TEXT,
    loser_ht INT,
    loser_id INT,
    loser_ioc TEXT,
    loser_name TEXT,
    loser_rank INT,
    loser_rank_points INT,
    loser_seed INT,
    match_num INT,
    minutes INT,
    round TEXT,
    score TEXT,
    surface TEXT,
    tourney_date DATE,
    tourney_id TEXT,
    tourney_level TEXT,
    tourney_name TEXT,
    winner_age FLOAT,
    winner_entry TEXT,
    winner_hand TEXT,
    winner_ht INT,
    winner_id INT,
    winner_ioc TEXT,
    winner_name TEXT,
    winner_rank INT,
    winner_rank_points INT,
    winner_seed INT,
    year INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (winner_id) REFERENCES players(player_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (loser_id) REFERENCES players(player_id)
);

CREATE TABLE rankings (
    ranking_date DATE,
    ranking INT,
    player_id INT,
    ranking_points INT,
    tours INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (player_id) REFERENCES players(player_id)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

```sql
SELECT *
FROM matches
WHERE minutes IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY minutes DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
there should be a winner of the match involved in this

```sql
SELECT
    winner_id,
    winner_name,
    loser_id,
    loser_name,
    tourney_name,
    tourney_date,
    round,
    score,
    minutes
FROM matches
WHERE minutes IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY minutes DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
we should check out the players who played in that match

```sql
WITH longest_match AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM matches
    WHERE minutes IS NOT NULL
    ORDER BY minutes DESC
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
    'winner' AS match_role,
    p.player_id,
    p.first_name,
    p.last_name,
    p.hand,
    p.birth_date,
    p.country_code,
    lm.tourney_name,
    lm.tourney_date,
    lm.round,
    lm.score,
    lm.minutes
FROM longest_match lm
JOIN players p
    ON p.player_id = lm.winner_id

UNION ALL

SELECT
    'loser' AS match_role,
    p.player_id,
    p.first_name,
    p.last_name,
    p.hand,
    p.birth_date,
    p.country_code,
    lm.tourney_name,
    lm.tourney_date,
    lm.round,
    lm.score,
    lm.minutes
FROM longest_match lm
JOIN players p
    ON p.player_id = lm.loser_id;
```
We also need to get the names of both players in that match.

```sql
SELECT
    m.tourney_name,
    m.tourney_date,
    m.round,
    m.score,
    m.minutes,
    wp.player_id AS winner_id,
    wp.first_name AS winner_first_name,
    wp.last_name AS winner_last_name,
    lp.player_id AS loser_id,
    lp.first_name AS loser_first_name,
    lp.last_name AS loser_last_name
FROM matches m
JOIN players wp
    ON wp.player_id = m.winner_id
JOIN players lp
    ON lp.player_id = m.loser_id
WHERE m.minutes IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY m.minutes DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
we also need the name of the loser in that match

```sql
SELECT
    m.tourney_name,
    m.tourney_date,
    m.round,
    m.score,
    m.minutes,
    wp.player_id AS winner_id,
    wp.first_name || ' ' || wp.last_name AS winner_name,
    lp.player_id AS loser_id,
    lp.first_name || ' ' || lp.last_name AS loser_name
FROM matches m
JOIN players wp
    ON wp.player_id = m.winner_id
JOIN players lp
    ON lp.player_id = m.loser_id
WHERE m.minutes IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY m.minutes DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
